title: Capital Gains Exemption: Two Adjoining Flats as One Home Under Section 54F
description: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) recently ruled on claiming capital gains tax exemption for buying two adjoining flats. This ruling clarifies that two.

faq.q: Can I claim Section 54F exemption if I buy two separate flats in different buildings?
faq.a: No, the ITAT ruling specifically refers to "adjoining" flats that are physically connected and used as a single residence. Buying separate flats in different buildings would not qualify.

faq.q: What if I don't physically connect the two adjoining flats?
faq.a: If the flats are not physically connected and continue to function as two separate, independent units, they will likely not be considered a "single residential house" for Section 54F exemption purposes. Physical integration is key.

faq.q: Is this ITAT ruling a new law?
faq.a: No, ITAT rulings are interpretations of existing law. They provide clarity on how the Income Tax Act should be applied in specific situations. While not a new law, it sets a precedent for similar cases.

faq.q: What kind of documentation do I need to prove single usage?
faq.a: You should gather architectural plans showing the merged layout, invoices for renovation work, utility bills (if they reflect combined usage), and photographs of the integrated living space.

faq.q: Can NRIs also claim this exemption?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are also eligible to claim capital gains exemptions under Section 54F, provided they meet all the specified conditions, including the reinvestment in a residential house in India.

faq.q: Does this ruling apply to Section 54 as well?
faq.a: While the ruling specifically addresses Section 54F, the principle of treating physically integrated adjoining flats as one residential unit has been upheld in some cases for Section 54 as well by various courts. However, it's always best to consult a tax expert for specific advice.
